question: If I quit school partway through the quarter, will the classes I was taking show up on my transcript?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 113 Withdrawals > 1. Withdrawal from the University

reference_answer: It depends on timing. Leaving before the quarter starts leaves nothing on the transcript; leaving in the first 14 calendar days records only the withdrawal date; after that, every course held at the time is marked RD along with the date. Withdrawal is possible until the last day of instruction but not once finals begin.

question: What if the reason I'm leaving is that I've been called up for active military duty?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 113 Withdrawals > 2. Withdrawal from the University for Military Service

reference_answer: Students who are drafted or called to active duty can take a military withdrawal. Leaving by the end of week seven gives a full fee refund and no credit; leaving later lets the student pick either a full refund or credit with grades reported by instructors. Students who enlist voluntarily follow the normal withdrawal rules.
notes: Follow-up: relies on q001 for the withdrawal context.

question: What does an RD grade mean on a UW transcript?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 110 Grades, Honors, and Scholarship > 1. The Grading System > A. System of Grades > 5. The Grade RD
SGP 113 Withdrawals > 3. Dropping a Course
SGP 113 Withdrawals > 1. Withdrawal from the University

reference_answer: RD means Registrar Drop. It marks a course dropped after day 14 of the quarter, and every course a student held when withdrawing from the University after that point. RD does not affect the grade-point average.

question: I got sick near the end of the quarter and can't finish my final project. Can my professor give me more time to complete the class?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 110 Grades, Honors, and Scholarship > 1. The Grading System > A. System of Grades > 3. The Grade I

reference_answer: The instructor may award an Incomplete (I) if your work was satisfactory up to about three weeks before the quarter ended and circumstances stop you from finishing, but is never obliged to. A final grade must be submitted by the next quarter's grading deadline or the I turns into 0.0; the instructor can ask the Registrar for one more quarter.

question: What about graduate students?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 110 Grades, Honors, and Scholarship > 1. The Grading System > B. Grading Practices for Graduate Students > 2. The Grade I

reference_answer: Graduate students can get an Incomplete on the same terms, but if no grade is submitted by the next quarter's deadline the I stays on the record permanently instead of becoming 0.0. To earn credit they must finish the work by the last day of the following quarter (summer excluded), and the instructor may seek one further quarter from the Registrar.
notes: Follow-up: relies on q004 for the Incomplete context.

question: Would I get in trouble for using an online solutions manual on my homework if my instructor never said it was allowed?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 209 Student Conduct Policy for Academic Misconduct and Behavioral Misconduct > 7. Prohibited Conduct > C. Academic Misconduct

reference_answer: Yes. Relying on an answer key or solution manual found online, without the instructor's OK, counts as cheating under the student conduct policy, which makes it academic misconduct.

question: What puts an undergraduate on Academic Warning status?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 107 Low Academic Standing and Academic Dismissal > 3. Academic Warning Status
SGP 107 Low Academic Standing and Academic Dismissal > 2. Academic Alert Status

reference_answer: A continuing undergraduate goes on Academic Warning when the cumulative GPA drops below 2.00. A student placed on Academic Alert after a first quarter under 2.00 also moves to Academic Warning if the cumulative GPA is still below 2.00 after the second quarter.

question: How does a student get a Travel Warning Waiver for official UW travel to a high-risk country?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 211 Student International Travel Policy > 5. Restrictions on Travel to High Risk Destinations and Travel Warning Waivers

reference_answer: The student applies through the waiver review process. Each request is judged case by case, reviewed by the travel risk committee (ITRASC), and must be approved by the Provost before departure. Students who travel to such places without a waiver count as independent travelers and may get no University help in an emergency.

question: What is a conduct hold, and what can it stop a student from doing?

expected.heading_prefix: SGP 209 Student Conduct Policy for Academic Misconduct and Behavioral Misconduct > 10. Initiating Conduct Proceedings > J. Conduct Hold on Student Record

SGP 210 Student Conduct Policy for Discriminatory and Sexual Harassment, Intimate Partner Violence, Sexual Misconduct, Stalking, and Retaliation > 10. Initiating Conduct Proceedings > J. Conduct Hold on Student Record

reference_answer: A conduct hold is a flag a conduct office may place on a student's record while a misconduct report or proceeding is pending, or to monitor a sanction. Until it is lifted it can block class registration, ordering an official transcript, or earning a degree. A hold does not mean the student has been found responsible.
notes: The same rule appears in both student conduct policies (SGP 209 and SGP 210).

question: Can staff ask someone with a guide dog what their disability is, or demand proof that the dog is certified?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 46.6 – Service Animals > 4. Assessing Service Animal Status > A. Permitted Inquiries

reference_answer: No. When the animal's role is not obvious, staff may ask only whether it is needed because of a disability and what task it has been trained to do. They may not ask about the disability itself or require medical records, registration, an ID card, or a demonstration.

question: Are there situations where they can make the person take the animal out of the building?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 46.6 – Service Animals > 13. Removal of Animals from University Facilities

reference_answer: Yes. The University can require removal of an animal that is left unattended, poses a direct threat to others' health or safety, is not housebroken, is out of control, or is seriously unclean. The handler must be allowed to come back without the animal, and an exclusion applies only to the event where the problem happened.
notes: Follow-up: relies on q010 for the service animal context.

question: Is it okay to text my kids or book a dentist appointment from my work computer?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 47.2 – Personal Use of University Facilities, Computers, and Equipment by University Employees > 1. Policy > B. Criteria for Limited Personal Use

reference_answer: Generally yes. Employees may make occasional personal use of University computers if it costs the state little or nothing, is short and infrequent, does not get in the way of others' official work, and does not put state property or information at risk. Contacting dependents and scheduling personal appointments are listed as acceptable examples.

question: Could my department install a security camera in our office to check whether people are actually working?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 13.5 – Regulating the Installation and Use of Security Cameras > Policy Statements > 1. General Provisions

reference_answer: No. Cameras installed for security can't be used to assess or keep watch on staff, and they cannot go in places where people reasonably expect privacy, such as private offices, restrooms, or locker rooms.

question: I work full-time at UW. Can I take classes without paying full tuition?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 22.1 – Tuition Waivers and the Tuition Exemption Program for UW and State Employees > Policy Statements > 4. Tuition Exemption Program for UW and State Employees: Information and Eligibility

reference_answer: Likely yes. Through the Tuition Exemption Program, eligible employees working at least half-time who are admitted as students can get up to six credits of tuition waived each quarter, when space is available, at the Seattle, Bothell, and Tacoma campuses. Some courses and programs are excluded, and credits beyond six are charged per credit.

question: A coworker is going through cancer treatment and has used up her sick time. Can I give her some of my vacation hours?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 45.10 – Shared Leave Program for Time Off Accruing Staff, Students, Librarians, and Educators > 4. Request to Donate or Receive Shared Leave

reference_answer: Yes, through the Shared Leave Program. Employees can donate leave to a colleague with a severe or life-threatening illness or injury who has used, or is about to use, their paid time off, following state and University procedures.

question: Under APS 2.4, what are system owners responsible for?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 2.4 Information Security and Privacy: Roles, Responsibilities, and Definitions > 2. Roles and Responsibilities Related to Information Security, Privacy, or Data Protection > H. System Owners

reference_answer: System owners oversee building, running, and maintaining an information system, including designing in privacy and security controls for the information in their area. They also tell the leaders of major University units what resources are needed to protect that information.

question: Can student or hourly employees get a cell phone allowance under APS 55.1?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 55.1 – Mobile Device Use and Allowance Policy > 5. Ineligible Individuals

reference_answer: Normally no. Student, temporary, and hourly employees cannot receive a University phone or an allowance for a personal device, though an appointing authority may grant a documented, time-limited exception. Staff on unpaid leave or on appointments shorter than twelve months get nothing for months they do not work.

question: How long does a state employee whistleblower have to file a retaliation complaint?

expected.heading_prefix: APS 47.1 – Summary of the State Employee Whistleblower Act > 5. Whistleblower Protection

reference_answer: Two years. A whistleblower who suffers reprisal can bring a claim to the state Human Rights Commission, and retaliation is presumed unless the employer proves it acted for unrelated, legitimate reasons.

question: Is a professor allowed to date a student who is in their class?

expected.heading_prefix: EO No. 54 Employee–Student Romantic Relationships and Conflicts of Interest > 2. Policy

reference_answer: Not unless it is managed. University employees may not date a student when the relationship creates a real or apparent conflict of interest, or hold authority over a student they are or were involved with, unless an acceptable management plan is in place.

question: If I talk to the ombud's office about a conflict at work, will they keep what I say confidential?

expected.heading_prefix: EO No. 18 The University Ombud > 5. Use of Information

reference_answer: Largely yes. The Ombud treats information discreetly and shares sensitive details only when the law requires it or a compelling public interest is at stake, such as possible illegal activity or risk of harm, and then with the person's knowledge where possible.

question: I volunteer at a UW summer camp and a child said something that makes me think they're being abused at home. Who do I have to tell, and how quickly?

expected.heading_prefix: EO No. 56 Reporting Suspected Child Abuse or Neglect > 5. Reporting Process
SGP 209 Student Conduct Policy for Academic Misconduct and Behavioral Misconduct > 3. Privacy and Confidentiality > C. Reporting Suspected Child Abuse

reference_answer: You must phone the police or DSHS, the state social services agency, at the first opportunity, and no more than 48 hours after you have reasonable cause to suspect abuse; call 911 in an emergency. The duty covers University employees and volunteers alike.

question: If I invent something as an undergrad, does the University automatically own it?

expected.heading_prefix: EO No. 36 Inventions, Discoveries, and Copyright > Definitions > 1. Rights and Responsibilities of Employees and Students Upon Realization of Inventions and Discoveries When the University Has an Ownership Interest > B. Students

reference_answer: No. Students own their inventions unless, for example, the invention comes from their University job, from University-administered research money or heavy use of University facilities and resources, from a sponsored project, or from a faculty-led project using non-public information, or they signed an assignment agreement. Normal coursework use of labs, computers, and libraries is not substantial use.

question: Who decides whether the Seattle campus closes because of snow or wildfire smoke?

expected.heading_prefix: AO 107 Delegation of Authority for Taking Necessary Actions to Protect the University’s Interests and Operations in Response to an Emergency Situation > 2. Authority to Suspend Operations

reference_answer: For UW Seattle, a weather advisory group meets and recommends to the President whether to suspend operations, start late, or close early because of severe winter weather, heat, or smoke. The decision to suspend operations rests with the President.

question: Under the Outside Professional Work Policy, how much paid consulting can full-time faculty do?

expected.heading_prefix: EO No. 57 Outside Professional Work Policy > 2. Outside Consulting Activities > B. Time Limitations

reference_answer: With advance approval, up to 13 calendar days in each academic quarter of employment, about one day a week. With prior approval the days can be averaged over the academic year, but consulting may not interfere with teaching, other assignments, or grant commitments.

question: What privileges come with a Visiting Scholar Identification Card?

expected.heading_prefix: EO No. 39 Athletic Tickets, Identification Cards, and Campus Privileges > 5. Visiting Scholar Identification Card

reference_answer: Issued by a dean for at most one academic year, the card gives visiting scholars library borrowing, access to study and non-classified research facilities and ASUW recreation facilities, Faculty Club participation, and campus parking at a prorated fee. It does not make free any privilege that regular faculty pay for.

question: What must each school's or college's procedure under Executive Order 58 on student academic grievances include?

expected.heading_prefix: EO No. 58 Student Academic Grievance Procedures > 2. General Provisions

reference_answer: Every unit's procedure must offer an informal conciliation step (with help available from the Ombud), a grievance committee of faculty and students, hearing procedures that produce advisory recommendations to the dean, and an appeal of the dean's decision to the Provost.

question: Under Administrative Order 107, who can order a shutdown of the Husky Network?

expected.heading_prefix: AO 107 Delegation of Authority for Taking Necessary Actions to Protect the University’s Interests and Operations in Response to an Emergency Situation > 3. Authority to Shut Down the Husky Network

reference_answer: Either the President or UW-IT's vice president, who also serves as the University CIO, may order it to limit the loss of critical data during a cybersecurity incident. The CIO must consult the UW Medicine CIO before affecting UW Medicine networks, and must report the shutdown to the President promptly.

question: Can the UW take back a degree after it has already been awarded?

expected.heading_prefix: Regent Policy No. 31 – Revocation of Degrees

reference_answer: Yes. On the faculty's recommendation, the Board of Regents can revoke a degree when the graduate did not meet its standards. If fraud concealed the problem there is no time limit; otherwise revocation must happen within two years and must not cause undue hardship.

question: If I sign up to speak at a Board of Regents meeting, how long do I get?

expected.heading_prefix: Article III—Meetings of the Board > 12. Public Comment Period

reference_answer: Each public comment normally gets two minutes, and the whole comment period is capped at ten minutes, though the Chair can extend either. Speakers sign up in advance through the Regents' online form, must use their own name, and cannot hand their time to someone else.

question: Does the president need to check with the Regents before the University sues a city or another public agency?

expected.heading_prefix: Chapter 1 Delegation of Authority > 7. Commencement of Legal Action

reference_answer: The President can pursue legal action to protect the University on the Board's behalf, but suing a public entity or official, or using eminent domain, first requires consulting the Board Chair, or the Vice Chair if the Chair is absent.

question: What does a proposal to rename a building need under the Regents' Naming Policy?

expected.heading_prefix: Regent Policy No. 50 – Naming Policy > 8. Renaming
Regent Policy No. 50 – Naming Policy > 4. Honorific Naming

reference_answer: It needs everything required for an honorific naming plus a history of the original name, a recommendation on memorializing the old name (or why that is unnecessary), and support from bodies like the Faculty Senate or student government. Renaming is conditional on approval by the Board or the President.

question: Under Regent Policy No. 11, what must a regent with a beneficial interest in a University transaction do?

expected.heading_prefix: Regent Policy No. 11 – Policy Regarding Regent Conflicts of Interest > 2. Specific Transactions

reference_answer: The regent must fully disclose the nature of the interest and stay out of the board's discussion and vote on that transaction, as the state Ethics in Public Service Act requires.

question: Can the ASUW or the Faculty Senate send a representative to sit with the Board of Regents?

expected.heading_prefix: Article VI—Student, Faculty, and Alumni Representatives > 1. Designated Representatives

reference_answer: Yes. ASUW, GPSS, the Bothell and Tacoma student associations, the Faculty Senate, and the Alumni Association may each name one representative a year to sit with the Board at public meetings, and at committee meetings when invited. Each organization pays its own representative's costs.

question: Our student group wants to put a sculpture on the lawn outside our building for a few months. Who has to approve it?

expected.heading_prefix: Chapter 205 Campus Art Policies > 4. General Operating Procedures > E. Review Process for Temporary Installations (One Year or Less)

reference_answer: For temporary outdoor art, a sponsoring unit takes the proposal to a University representative, who checks safety and installation, and then to one or more campus reviewing bodies, which can approve or reject it. Temporary indoor pieces need only the sign-off of the department administrator or building coordinator, who may ask for further review.
notes: Source is Employment and Administrative Policies Chapter 205, published with Board of Regents governance.

question: On what grounds can a tenured professor be fired?

expected.heading_prefix: FCG Chapter 25 Tenure of the Faculty > Section 25-51 Grounds for Removal of Persons with Tenure for Cause
FCG Chapter 25 Tenure of the Faculty > Section 25-52 Removal of Faculty for Reasons of Program Elimination

reference_answer: Removal for cause is limited to incompetence, neglect of duty, incapacity to do academic work, unlawful discrimination or sexual harassment, scholarly misconduct, a felony conviction, or deliberate interference with others' academic work, and the conduct must substantially impair the person's University duties. Tenured faculty can also be removed when their program is eliminated, under separate procedures.

question: How much paid time off does a faculty member get after having or adopting a baby?

expected.heading_prefix: FCG Chapter 51 Faculty Leave and Vacations > Section 51-11 Paid Faculty Sick and Parental Leave > H. Parental Leave

reference_answer: Faculty can take up to 90 days of paid parental leave as one continuous block within 12 months of a birth, adoption, or new guardianship of a child under 18. Twins or several children placed at once count as a single event.

question: Would taking that leave push back my tenure review?

expected.heading_prefix: FCG Chapter 51 Faculty Leave and Vacations > Section 51-11 Paid Faculty Sick and Parental Leave > H. Parental Leave

reference_answer: It can. A request to extend the mandatory review clock for a birth, adoption, or guardianship is always approved, within the Provost's overall limits on extensions, and the faculty member does not have to take the leave to qualify.
notes: Follow-up: relies on q036 for the parental leave context.

question: Which faculty appointment types do not lead to tenure under the Faculty Code?

expected.heading_prefix: FCG Chapter 25 Tenure of the Faculty > Section 25-32 Criteria for Tenure

reference_answer: Tenure is not earned under acting, visiting, lecturer, artist in residence, teaching associate, professor of practice, adjunct, research, teaching, clinical, clinical practice, or affiliate appointments, nor under appointments marked as non-tenure or not paid from regular University funds, unless the President states otherwise in writing.

question: Does the Faculty Code's open access policy give the University copyright in faculty articles?

expected.heading_prefix: FCG Chapter 54 Open Access > Section 54-41 Policy and Grant of Rights
FCG Chapter 54 Open Access > Section 54-51 Scope and Waiver

reference_answer: No. Faculty give the University a broad, permanent, nonexclusive license so their scholarly articles can be shared freely in an open access repository, but they keep ownership of the copyright. The Provost must waive the license or delay access for a particular article whenever the author asks.

question: Does the Faculty Regent represent the Faculty Senate on the Board of Regents?

expected.heading_prefix: FCG Chapter 45 The Faculty Regent > Section 45-31 Responsibility and Limitations of the Faculty Regent

reference_answer: No. State law requires one regent to be a faculty member, but as a board member the Faculty Regent acts for the public of Washington state rather than for the faculty or the Senate. The Senate Chair speaks for the Faculty Senate at Regents meetings.
